title: The Favorite-Longshot Bias in Prediction Markets: Evidence from Polymarket
abstract: arXiv:2609.12878v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The favorite--longshot bias (FLB) is one of the most persistent return patterns in betting markets, but its prevalence in modern prediction markets and its relation to recurrent longshot demand remain unclear. We study these questions in Polymarket, a large and increasingly important prediction market, using 588 million trades by 2.48 million accounts. In observed transaction flows, purchases below 10 cents lose 19.3 cents per dollar, while purchases at or above 90 cents earn 0.83 cents. How contracts are grouped changes the result: longshots lose 6.3 cents per dollar when each contract is weighted equally but gain 4.1 cents when related contracts are first grouped by parent event; the two-sided pattern is robust in Crypto and Politics but surprisingly absent in Sports. translated_title: 预测市场中的热门-冷门偏差：来自Polymarket的证据
translated_abstract: 热门-冷门偏差（FLB）是博彩市场中最持久的收益模式之一，但它在现代预测市场中的普遍程度及其与反复出现的冷门需求之间的关系仍不清楚。我们在Polymarket——一个规模庞大且日益重要的预测市场——中研究这些问题，使用了来自248万个账户的5.88亿笔交易数据。在观察到的交易流中，低于10美分的买入每美元亏损19.3美分，而90美分及以上的买入每美元赚取0.83美分。合约的分组方式会改变结果：当每个合约权重相等时，冷门合约每美元亏损6.3美分，但当相关合约先按父事件分组时则每美元盈利4.1美分；这种双边模式在加密货币和政治类别中稳健存在，但在体育类别中却意外缺失。过去最倾向于购买冷门合约的前十分之一账户占下月低价买入总额的26.6%，但其收益与其他账户相似。
tldr: 该论文利用Polymarket上248万账户的5.88亿笔交易数据，首次系统揭示了预测市场中的热门-冷门偏差，发现低价合约显著亏损、该模式依赖合约分组方式且存在于加密货币和政治市场而非体育市场，且最强冷门偏好者贡献了大量低价买入却未获得超额收益。
en_tdlr: Using 588 million trades from 2.48 million accounts on Polymarket, this paper documents the favorite-longshot bias in prediction markets, showing that low-priced purchases lose substantially, the pattern depends on contract grouping and holds in Crypto and Politics but not Sports, and the strongest longshot buyers drive most low-price demand without earning superior returns.
